title: Status of the fingertip, contact-model and DIP-link work
lede: On 2026-10-18 the owner asked for nine things in one window: push everything, keep autopilot runs off the Max seat, a print procedure, a calibration of Drake's field and the pads to the finite elements (FE), the capsule and quarter-ellipsoid prints if they can be modelled, a DIP-link redesign that clamps the magnetometer board against the printed tip, and a file-explorer layout for the page index; at the printer the owner chose the 2.9 mm magnet seat. Pushing, the autopilot default, the procedure, the 2.9 mm print set and the page tree are done. The calibration ran: no print meets every criterion. The DIP link has two complete designs; a third, the judge, the final design and its page run as a job on the personal login.

sections.heading: Prints at the 2.9 mm seat
paras: Print order and the steps at each pause are on the [print procedure](experiments/20261018-fingertip_print_procedure/20261018-siraya85a_fingertip_print_procedure.html). The curved tips' pauses are 0.1 mm lower than in the 2.7 mm set (9.2 and 16.2 mm). Record each print in `docs/experiments/20261018-fingertip_print_procedure/records/prints.csv`; the seat result is in `records/seat_coupon.csv`. These tips fit the current DIP link; concept a needs two dovetail channels in the tip's back face and concept b cuts the tip's dorsal 6 mm away, so either redesign needs reprinted tips.

sections.heading: Calibration of Drake's field and the pads to the finite elements
paras: Calibration to the FE works for stiffness and twist arm on the half-ellipsoids, and the two simulators still disagree on their turns; no print meets every criterion of the plan (`docs/experiments/20261018-fe_contact_calibration/plan.json`: approach within 25 % RMS, twist arm 0.70-1.15 times the FE's, pads and Drake ending their iCEM turns on the same branch as often as on the block).

Approach: the tip's travel toward the palm under a probe, from the FE of the 85A prints at 30 % gyroid with four 3 x 2 mm magnets, under rods of 5, 8 and 12.5 mm radius at 0.5, 1 and 3 N. Twist arm: the pressure-weighted patch radius that sets the torque resisting a turn. M1: one modulus fitted to the approach; M3: a series spring in front of a stiff local field. One modulus leaves 20-24 % RMS approach error in Drake because Drake's pressure depends only on the local overlap, so its approach grows with about the square root of the force, while the printed shell over gyroid spreads the load and its approach grows with the 0.75-0.81 power of the force.

Pads and Drake on the 11/22 half-ellipsoid's iCEM turns: both hold the tool in 6 of 6 runs and finish 15-51 deg apart, against the pads' own seed spread of 0.58 deg; on a plan made for that tip they finish 32.5 deg apart. The pads creep 0.86-0.96 deg/s at 1 N where Drake creeps 0.004-0.012 deg/s, and pads at impratio 1000 still finish 0 of 6 on Drake's branch, so the cause is open. Drake replays took 50-180 s each against the 15 s planned, so the block and capsule consistency runs were cut. The block remains the tip on which the two agree (1.4 deg on the D1-D8 replays of 2026-10-16).

sections.heading: DIP-link redesign for the magnetometer board
paras: Two designs are complete and a third nearly so, each with STEP and STL files, a clearance check over PIP -18 to 92 deg and a sensing estimate. Concept a keeps the tip's outer surface: the DIP link's plate becomes a 0.85 mm window plate whose windows let the five MLX90393 chips stand 0.05 mm proud against the tip's back face, and a 3 mm dorsal clamp plate sandwiches the board with two M1.6 countersunk screws, two M2 screws and two locating pins. Concept b replaces the tip's dorsal 6 mm with a rigid cassette: four M1.6 screws and brass nuts clamp the board between a 0.9 mm PLA cover and a 3.6 mm tongue of the DIP link, and an 11 mm 85A pad snaps onto two dovetail rails; the pad keeps the palmar and side surfaces, halves the magnet travel per newton and raises the tip's modulus by 20 %, and the closer chips need GAIN_SEL 0-1. Concept c places the board at a print pause and prints a PLA cap and the TPU tip over it; its agent died after the CAD, the sensing estimate and most clearances, before the renders and the commit.

The specification (`docs/experiments/20261018-dip_link_board_mount/spec.json`) sets two hard constraints. The board's JST SH connector clashes with the MCP link by 1.45 mm at this placement, so the tab is cut to 4.9 mm or less and the cable soldered. One micrometre of board motion toward the magnets reads as 0.16 N of normal force with the chips on the back face, so the clamp must remove play below a micrometre. Both designs leave the 20 mm board 2.6 mm past each side of the 14.8 mm tip (rigid rim 3.1 mm), where the readiness study's board edge touched the cylinder in most HOM runs; a narrower board is the remedy the designs cannot provide.

Next, in the personal job: concept c's checks (step 3), the judge and the final design with a dimensioned drawing (step 4), the DIP page (step 5). The owner chooses the design after the judge's recommendation.

sections.heading: Resuming from this page
paras: `~/.claude/autopilot/ap status` shows the jobs and the usage of each login; `ap steps <job>` prints a job's ledger; `ap step add <job> "text"` gives a running job a new step and `--rule` a standing direction; `tmux attach -r -t ap-<job>` watches a session.

Rebuild this page with `.venv/bin/python scripts/status_page.py`; the curated text is `docs/status.json`, everything under a live heading is read from the autopilot kit, the print sheets, the DIP evaluations, INDEX.md, git and `~/.claude/resguard_events.jsonl` at build time. A session that finishes a step updates the matching row of `docs/status.json` and rebuilds.
